label: H.R. 10204
title: Legislative Branch Agencies Clarification Act

items.snippet: This bill revises the procedures for appointing and removing the Librarian of Congress, the Director of the Government Publishing Office (GPO), and the Register of Copyrights.

items.item: Director of the Government Publishing Office (GPO)
items.snippet: This bill revises the procedures for appointing and removing the Librarian of Congress, the Director of the Government Publishing Office (GPO), and the Register of Copyrights.
The bill also establishes an Office of Inspector General within the Copyright Office and requires GPO to establish a human management system.
The bill also establishes an Office of Inspector General within the Copyright Office and requires GPO to establish a human management system.
(Currently, these positions are appointed by the President with the advice and consent of the Senate.) The Librarian of Congress and the Director of GPO may only be…
The bill requires subordinate officers and employees of the Copyright Office to be appointed by the Register.
Further, the bill requires the Register (instead of the Librarian) to appoint the three administrative judges of the Copyright Royalty Board.

lobbying.caption: From Senate lobbying disclosures (LD-2). A filing mentions this bill; it does not show what was asked for, which side the client took, or any contact with this member. Reported amounts cover the whole filing, not this bill alone.
lobbying.amount_note: Amounts are the income or expenses reported on the whole LD-2 filing, not money spent on this bill.

caption: This shows who the bill names and who lobbied on it. It does not show who gains or loses, and lobbying can be for or against a bill.

G000568.label: Overlap, not proof of influence.
G000568.caption: Money from this member's itemized individual donors (over $200) whose self-reported employer falls in an industry that also has a client lobbying on this bill. Correlation only; not a quid pro quo. Donors give to campaigns for many reasons, and a lobbying client may have opposed the bill.
